title: settings.v1: a person's own settings, the file $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/recursion/settings.toml
description: The shape of the TOML file once it is parsed. One owner-only file of the person's own; the core reads it (recursion_core/settings.py) and nothing of the product writes it. Every setting has a default, so the file and every key in it may be absent. The list of settings is append-only: a later version adds properties and never renames or removes one. A key this version does not declare is reported by the reader (settings_unknown_key) and skipped, so additional properties are allowed here. A value of the wrong type or below its meaningful floor keeps the default (settings_value_out_of_range). Numeric advice does not constrain the value in force. A numeric setting can opt in to the reserved string 'none' for no limit. List settings take arrays of strings, with repeated names read once in first-occurrence order. Each leaf's 'default' and 'description' are those of the reader's table. The settings file reader accepts version only as a TOML integer (a whole number such as 1) and rejects a float such as 1.0.

gil_check.description: Whether each plugin host makes its GIL check; on by default, and a person may turn it off.

plugins.description: Plugins listed here may keep saved data between runs. Recursion keeps it for them in its own state folder; no other plugin can read it, and Recursion never hands it to a task it runs, though the plugin itself may put what it saved into a task it asks for. Read when Recursion starts. Empty as shipped.

max_bytes_per_plugin.description: The most saved data one plugin may keep, keys and values together, in bytes; none for no limit.

max_item_bytes.description: The largest one item of a plugin's saved data may be, in bytes; held to what fits one message between Recursion and a plugin, and shown so; none means only that bound.

max_items_per_plugin.description: The most items of saved data one plugin may keep; none for no limit.

list_page_max.description: The most keys one listing of a plugin's saved data answers; none means as many as fit one message.

calls_per_minute.description: The most calls on its saved data one plugin may make in one minute; none for no limit.

sync.description: How each write of saved data reaches the disk: full waits for the disk; normal is faster and may lose the last writes if the power fails. Any other text reads as full.

wal_max_bytes.description: How large the write-ahead file of a plugin's saved data may grow, in bytes, before Recursion folds it into the store ahead of the next write; none for no limit.

record_each_write.description: Whether every write and delete of saved data leaves a record row; false leaves one summary when the plugin's host ends.

record_key_text.description: Whether a record row keeps the text of a saved-data key; false keeps only its SHA-256 and its length.
